//simulator: iOS SIMULATOR build. This profile did not exist, and its absence wasted a lot of time.
Every iOS build on record is distribution=STORE, isForIosSimulator=false. So testing
'through the simulator' could only have meant a locally-run dev build or Expo Go — and
NEITHER APPLIES EAS UPDATES. A dev client loads its bundle from Metro; Expo Go ignores
the project's update configuration entirely. Every `eas update` published to the
production branch was therefore invisible on that simulator, and round after round of
fixes were evaluated against whatever code happened to be in that build.
Two properties make this profile reflect what is actually shipped:
ios.simulator: true  — produces a .app runnable in the Simulator, and needs NO code
signing, so it cannot fail on credentials.
channel: production  — binds it to the SAME update branch the OTA workflow publishes
to, so an `eas update` reaches it exactly as it reaches a real
build. A different channel here would recreate the original
`developmentClient` is deliberately absent: with it, the app loads from Metro and
ignores updates again, which is the very thing being fixed.
